allEvents.after:
The elder's hand rose for the warding gesture, his fingers already tracing the first curve of the binding sigil meant to lock the failure in place. I broke the band across my mouth with a sharp twist of my wrist, the leather snapping free so the next words could leave me clear. The accusation the elder had started to form died on his tongue as I spoke the invocation syllable aloud, forcing the final thread of the rite into the open air where any hidden misalignment could be measured.

The family at the canopy's edge surged forward, their voices rising in a single wave of blame. They named me the interference, the one who had stepped between the youth and the elder's seal, the one who had dragged the failed wish upright instead of letting the price claim it cleanly. The elder's eyes narrowed further, the luminous violet of his pupils contracting as he turned the charge back on the youth herself, claiming the grass cooling under my palm could only have come from an ill-wish she had carried into the circle. The crowd's murmurs thickened, some naming Julian again, the one whose alignment-sense never wavered, the one they would call if the rite could not be salvaged without further loss.

I tried to name the twist I felt beneath my palm, the way the grass had shifted from crimson to a dull, resisting brown the moment the youth's voice warped. The words would not arrange themselves. The misalignment was real, the bond between the youth and the wish fraying in a pattern I had never encountered, yet I could offer no cause, no source, no name that would satisfy the circle. My heel pressed harder into the spiralgrass, the blades yielding only enough to show the pressure and no more.

The elder's shadow lengthened across both of us. "The rite is sealed," he said, voice low and final. "Any further interference will be read as defiance of the public safeguard."

The youth's eyes had gone fully translucent, her weight sagging against my grip. I held her upright, my alignment-sense still flaring hot against the sour thread, and the crowd's accusations circled tighter. Someone at the edge called for Julian by name, the syllables carrying the weight of precedent. The elder did not object. He simply waited, his thumb still circled the first sigil line he had drawn.

Julian arrived without announcement, the canopy parting around his presence as though the weave itself had already decided the matter. He moved through the gathered First Favored with the quiet intensity that always made the room feel smaller, his breath stirring the nearest blades of spiralgrass. The slight asymmetry of his mouth tightened when his gaze found the youth's rigid posture and the elder's unfinished sigil. He did not speak at once. His hand turned the signet ring on his finger once, the metal catching the low light that filtered through the willow veil-canopy.

I felt the shift the moment his eyes met mine across the youth's bowed head. The crowd's accusations had not reached him yet, but the tension had. He lowered himself beside me with visible reluctance, his knee knocking once against mine before he steadied it. His palm came to rest on the Alignment Circle etched into the spiralgrass, the contact deliberate and measured, as though the circle itself might resist him.

The decision pressed against my ribs before he spoke. I could demand the full weight of his alignment-sense, the complete examination that would bind him to the outcome as surely as the wish had bound the youth. Or I could accept the limited reach he offered now, the single hand on the circle, the refusal to commit beyond what the elder's summons required.

Julian's fingers spread across the etched lines. The grass beneath them darkened another shade, the grass cooling another shade under his touch with a slow, reluctant pulse. He did not look at me again. His attention stayed on the circle, the weight of what he was choosing to measure settling between us like another unspoken accusation.

I realize that old tarot deck is still in my hand. Reassuringly solid. Present. One of the heavy gold cards slips out — "Petition Fate" is inscribed on it. If only it were that easy. I would wish myself a way out. No — a way in.

The family at the canopy's edge surged forward, their voices rising in a single wave of blame. They named me the interference, the one who had stepped between the youth and the elder's seal, the one who had dragged the failed wish upright instead of letting the price claim it cleanly. The elder's eyes narrowed further, the luminous violet of his pupils contracting as he turned the charge back on the youth herself, claiming the grass cooling under my palm could only have come from an ill-wish she had carried into the circle. My heel pressed harder into the spiralgrass, the blades yielding only enough to show the pressure and no more.

The elder's shadow lengthened across both of us. "The rite is sealed," he said, voice low and final. "Any further interference will be read as defiance of the public safeguard."

I felt the shift the moment his eyes met mine across the youth's bowed head. The crowd's accusations had not reached him yet, but the tension had.
